title: Image to PDF: prepare images and check page sizes
excerpt: Convert JPG or PNG batches in the right order, understand image-sized pages and combine mixed formats safely.
author: The MY PDF FIX Team
body:
## Choose the converter that matches your files

Use [JPG to PDF](/jpg-to-pdf) for JPG or JPEG files and [PNG to PDF](/png-to-pdf) for PNG files. Each tool accepts multiple images of its own format and creates one PDF page per image. There is no mixed JPG-and-PNG batch in either interface.

JPG is often suitable for photographs. PNG avoids JPG compression artifacts in screenshots and line drawings. Neither format can restore text or details that are already blurred. Start with a source image you can read comfortably before converting it.

## Prepare a small practice batch

For example, choose three harmless receipt photos. Crop the surrounding table or background in an image editor first, check that no edge is cut off and turn each image upright. The PDF converter does not provide an image crop or perspective-correction editor.

1. Open the matching converter and add the images.
2. Inspect the displayed file order. If necessary, remove an image and re-add it to place it at the end.
3. Click **Process**, then **Download**.
4. Open the saved PDF and verify that it has three pages in the same order, with all receipt details readable.

Numbering filenames can help you recognize the intended order, but always check the actual list. A file picker may return a different sequence than you expected.

## Understand the output page size

The tools embed images at their original pixel dimensions and use those dimensions as PDF points for page width and height. For example, a 1200-by-1600-pixel image produces a 1200-by-1600-point page. Different image dimensions can create different page sizes within the same PDF.

There is no A4, Letter, margin or output-DPI picker in these converters. For a required paper size, prepare the document in an application with explicit page-layout controls. When printing an image-sized PDF, inspect the print preview and scaling settings rather than assuming it will fit the paper automatically.

## Combine JPG and PNG groups

Convert the JPG group and PNG group separately, then join their PDFs with [Merge PDF](/merge-pdf). If their pages must alternate, use [Reorder Pages](/reorder-pdf-pages) after merging. That requires a list containing every page exactly once.

For example, if the merged order is two JPG pages followed by one PNG page and you want the PNG in the middle, enter `1,3,2` in Reorder. Check the final page identities before sharing.

## Reduce size without promising a fixed saving

Image dimensions, compression and page content affect file size. There is no reliable fixed percentage saving from switching formats or removing color. If a result is too large, resize a copy of the source images and compare legibility, or try [Compress PDF](/compress-pdf). Recommended and Strong may rasterize pages; Light avoids that step.

Keep the originals. Browser memory limits large image batches, especially on phones. Conversion does not add OCR, so photographed words remain image content rather than selectable text.
